text: {"answer": "The evidence suggests remote work has a small positive effect on productivity overall, but the effect depends on the arrangement and the type of work. A meta-analysis of 82 studies found a small but positive average effect of working from home on employee productivity, driven by gains in hourly productivity and more hours worked [0a130e4f39dc#0]. A review of 50+ studies reports a median productivity impact of +10% for focused individual tasks but -4% for collaborative tasks [d658dc380b73#5]. Fully remote work has been linked to output reductions of 10-20% for some roles, especially collaboration-heavy ones or newly hired workers [d658dc380b73#6]. Hybrid schedules showed no measurable productivity difference from in-office peers in one randomized trial [d658dc380b73#5]. Personality also matters, as conscientiousness is positively associated with reported WFH productivity [44ecc13330bd#0]. Full-remote work has also been associated with reduced work productivity and worsening presenteeism [abefd158b9c2#2].
